transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Aaron Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Redwood CSM), Lisa Morales (Pioneer Head Procurement), Mark Riley (Pioneer InfoSec), Jenna Ortiz (Pioneer Legal), Samir Patel (Pioneer AI Platform)

[00:00] Aaron: hey everyone thanks for joining, happy holidays, we'll try to keep this tight. i'm aaron chen, account exec on the redwood side, joined by priya our solutions engineer and daniel who's going to support onboarding. can everyone quick intro?
[00:12] Lisa: lisa here, head of procurement at pioneer, i'll be owning the contracting side and coordinating with finance.
[00:20] Mark: mark, security -- i'll drive the SOC 2 and encryption questions.
[00:26] Jenna: jenna, legal, i'll be the one redlining.
[00:30] Samir: samir, platform, i'll validate integration and perf for our workloads.
[00:36] Priya: great, thanks. quick agenda: review current MSA/DPA points you flagged, SLA questions, pricing & PO path, and next steps for onboarding/pilot. sound good?
[00:45] Lisa: yes, that's exactly it.

[02:10] Aaron: to kick off, i saw the doc you sent with comments on data residency and audit logs. on redwood side, we support private deployments in VPC and offer customer-managed keys with KMS/HSM integrations; our hosted offering has configurable retention and we can limit logs on request.
[02:35] Mark: on KMS, is that envelope encryption with customer-managed keys or only provider? and how do you handle key rotation?
[02:45] Priya: it's customer-managed KMS in our private deployment and you can integrate your cloud KMS; for hosted we'll offer a bring-your-own-key option for enterprise tiers. key rotation is supported and we log rotation events to the audit trail; we can share implementation details in the SOC 2 docs.
[03:05] Mark: okay, please share the exact flow and where the keys are held.

[05:00] Jenna: on the DPA you stripped the liability cap lower than we can accept; we need to propose language for breach notifications and data subject requests, and a standard 72-hour notification window is required.
[05:20] Aaron: understood. our standard MSA has X cap and 72-hour notification; we'd be open to redlining specific carve-outs. we'll send a marked copy.
[05:35] Jenna: also need clarity on subprocessors and subprocessors list update cadence.
[05:40] Priya: we maintain a subprocessors registry and can commit to 30-days notice for additions; we can provide the current list in the docs.

[08:10] Samir: on performance -- our main ask is 99.9% availability SLA during business hours and p50 latency below 200ms for typical prompt sizes. is that realistic for hosted?
[08:30] Priya: for hosted, p50 under 200ms depends on model and token length; for curated smaller models we can hit that at typical request sizes. we recommend dedicated capacity for consistent p50 and p95 latency SLOs. dedicated pools give you predictable throughput and isolation which helps hit your 200ms goal.
[09:00] Aaron: we can propose SLA tiers, e.g., 99.9% uptime with credits, and a dedicated commitment for latency SLOs. pricing differs for hosted vs dedicated.

[11:10] Lisa: speaking of pricing, finance needs an approval path. we typically require a formal quote, PO terms, and invoice cadence (net30). do you accept vendor questionnaires (Next steps) and do you have an MSA signature page for our legal team?
[11:35] Aaron: yes we'll send a formal quote and an invoice/PO template; net30 is fine. we can also accept their vendor security questionnaire; i'll attach our responses.

[13:00] Mark: SOC 2 scope -- do you cover access controls for the full stack and do you provide penetration test reports?
[13:12] Priya: SOC 2 Type II is available, scope includes our control plane and hosted infra; for dedicated/private we provide guidance for your own SOC scoping. we also have pentest summaries and a vendor pen test report we can share under NDA.
[13:30] Mark: good, we will want SOC 2 plus evidence of patching cadence and incident response runbooks.

[16:40] Jenna: contractually we will need a clause about data deletion at contract termination and a certificate of destruction for persistent storage or a defined retention window.
[16:55] Priya: that's standard; DPA specifies data deletion timelines and we can include certs for dedicated hosts. we'll add the explicit language you prefer.

[19:20] Samir: integration question -- do you provide an SDK and sample terraform for private deployment? our infra team wants IaC and rollout docs.
[19:32] Daniel: yes, we have SDKs and Terraform modules for private and dedicated. we'll attach a starter repo and the onboarding checklist so you can map requirements to your infra.

[22:00] Lisa: procurement timeline: we need legal review, finance approval, and a security sign-off. estimate 3 weeks once we have redlined contracts. if we can get the MSA and pricing by Jan 2, purchasing hopes to issue a PO by Jan 23.
[22:20] Aaron: that's doable. we'll prioritize the redlines and pricing to hit that window.

[25:00] Jenna: one more on IP indemnity and model outputs -- we need language ensuring customer owns prompts and resulting outputs, and a limited representation around model behavior.
[25:15] Priya: we have a clause that customers retain rights to customer input and outputs; we can surface that explicitly and add a small paragraph on model behavior warnings.

[28:40] Mark: are there any cross-border data transfer concerns? we need EU residency for EU patients.
[28:50] Aaron: for EU data we can route requests to EU regions and support a private deployment in region; that will be in the DPA as a location commitment when required.

[31:10] Samir: for the pilot, we want to run a 2-week POC with 50k tokens/day, and test integration latency and correctness. will you provide a trial account and sandbox?
[31:25] Daniel: yes, we'll provision a trial environment and dedicated endpoint; priya will help set up traffic shaping and recommend model profiles.

[33:50] Lisa: regarding pricing approvals, we need volume tiers and an estimate for overage costs. also need clarity on token definitions and billing granularity.
[34:05] Aaron: we'll send a pricing sheet with volume tiers, overage rates, and token definitions. typical billing granularity is per 1k tokens and we provide monthly usage reports.

[36:40] Jenna: any third-party subprocessors that do inference or log storage? we need list and contractual assurances.
[36:55] Priya: inference kernels run on our infra partners; storage might be cloud object stores depending on deployment. we will provide the subprocessors list and contractual summary.

[39:10] Lisa: ok wrap up -- please recap next steps.
[39:20] Aaron: sure: we'll send redlined MSA/DPA by Jan 2, SOC2 and pentest artifacts by Jan 3, pricing and formal quote by Jan 2, and provision trial environment by Jan 5. schedule legal-only follow-up on Jan 6.
[39:40] Jenna: that sounds good. we'll circulate internal questions and aim to return redlines by Jan 10.
[40:00] Mark: and security will look at SOC2 and the subprocessors list as soon as available.
[40:10] Samir: i'll share our traffic profile and expected qps by Jan 4.

[45:00] Aaron: thanks everyone, we'll send the docs and follow up with calendar invites. happy holidays.
[45:10] Lisa: thanks all, bye.

Notes: transcription contains minor speaker attribution errors and occasional filler phrases; audio was clear overall. Shared links referenced during call: redwood SOC2 portal (link), onboarding checklist (link), pricing spreadsheet (link).
